title: Second trace reordering without a diagonal insertion
statement: Under the field, finiteness, localizing-closure, completed-reference and normalization hypotheses of [lem-sfb-rational-p1-second-ambient-contraction], take the invertibility witnesses hb,hp and an arrow epsilon with the original counit-component normalization. For M=q*K(1)[2], J_K followed by the inverse twist projection, twist of the inverse self-square exchange on M, and twist of q* of the literal counitComponent_K equals identity_M tensor the canonically transported trace2 followed by singleUnitIso.hom and the right unitor. No diagonal insertion, class, supported-source map or integral occurs in the equality. The exact equality is exposed as the sole field of [def-sfb-rational-p1-second-trace-equation]; this packaging changes no mathematical assertion.

proof.text: Open CounitComponentNormalized and replace epsilon by the literal counit. Factor it as counitProjectionPart followed by identity tensor the normalized scalar trace and the right unitor.
Obtain invertibility of beta and the scalar trace square from second_scalar_trace. Apply second_pretrace with that witness and the supplied hb,hp,hq.

For any monoidal F and braided target, prove naturality of the explicit strength and its compatibility with the right unitor from tensorator naturality, the monoidal right-unit law, braiding naturality and monoidal coherence. Conjugate by tensorShiftIso, whose naturality follows from the native shift comparison, to evaluate S_K,V against any scalar t:V→unit. Apply this to the normalized scalar trace. Multiply the scalar square by inverse beta and rewrite. This yields precisely the sole field of SecondTraceEquation.

proof_origin.place: Second identity; explicit tensor-naturality and unit-law assembly of the pretrace and scalar trace steps.

RationalP1AmbientComposites defines the maps but proves no contraction. The tower modules TowerP1TriangleFactorization, TowerP1SecondTraceReordering and TowerP1DiagonalProjectionFactor supply an analogous decomposition on a different tower-system category. The generic ringed section/projection and exchange/tensor theorems need normalization transport to the present internal-module category.
